parole.significato: A loose woolen tunic worn by men and women in Ancient Greece and in Ancient Rome.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek χιτών (khitṓn, “tunic”), from a Central Semitic *kittan, from the Akkadian 𒌆𒃰 (kitû, literally “flax, linen”), from Sumerian 𒄑𒃰 (kitû [GIŠ.GADA]).
From Ancient Greek νῆρος (nêros), from Akkadian 𒐞 (nēr).

parole.significato: A quantity of 3600, such as a period of 3600 years.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek σάρος (sáros), from Akkadian 𒊹 (šar₂ /⁠šār⁠/, “3600, total, many, a great quantity or measure”). parole.significato: A quantity of 60, such as a period of 60 years.
parole.testo: From Ancient Greek σῶσσος (sôssos), from Akkadian 𒋗𒅆 (šūši, “a unit of sixty”).
